setting.note: A bank clerk is arrested one morning for a crime never named, and spends a year being drawn deeper into a court that meets in attics and back rooms across an unnamed city built from Kafka's Prague.

rights.originalWork: In copyright in many territories through the 20th century; Franz Kafka wrote it 1914-1915 and it was published posthumously in 1925. This book is mapped as a cited work: we store none of its text and reproduce no passages. The places are facts and the notes are our own.
rights.translation: Originally written in German (Der Process). The place names here are our own English descriptions, not a quotation of any translation.
rights.textSource: None stored. A cited book reproduces no text.
rights.territoryNotes: Locations and original commentary only. No reproduction of the copyrighted text, in any territory.
rights.attribution: The Trial, Franz Kafka (1925). Locations mapped by Read the Places; not affiliated with or endorsed by the author's estate or publisher.

palette.note: The grey of case files and waiting rooms. A cited book's colour is not a quotation; this bureaucratic slate still clears WCAG AA on paper.
